identities.label: Korubo
identities.summary: The Korubo or Korubu, also known by the endonym Dslala and in Portuguese as caceteiros ('clubbers'), are a largely uncontacted, Panoan-speaking Indigenous people of Brazil living in the lower Vale do Javari in the western Amazon Basin. Much of what the outside world knows of this group is based on the research of Brazilian explorer Sydney Possuelo, who first contacted the tribe in October 1996, and journalist Paul Raffaele.
